title: Sheaf of modules associated to a module over the global sections
statement: Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism] and $R=\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$; for an open $U\subseteq X$ regard $\mathcal O_X(U)$ as an $R$-algebra through the restriction map $R=\mathcal O_X(X)\to\mathcal O_X(U)$. For an $R$-module $M$ let $\mathcal P_M$ be the presheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] with $\mathcal P_M(U)=\mathcal O_X(U)\otimes_RM$ (the base change of $M$ to $\mathcal O_X(U)$ [def-weil-module-base-change], an $\mathcal O_X(U)$-module through the factor $\mathcal O_X(U)$) and restriction maps $\rho^U_V\otimes\mathrm{id}_M$ for $V\subseteq U$. The *sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules associated to $M$* is the sheafification $\mathcal F_M=\mathcal P_M^\#$ [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], a sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with its $\mathcal O_X$-linear sheafification map $\sigma_M:\mathcal P_M\to\mathcal F_M$; its *canonical section map* is the $R$-linear map $c_M:M\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal F_M)$, $c_M(m)=\sigma_{M,X}(1\otimes m)$. For an $R$-linear map $u:M\to M'$, the maps $\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal O_X(U)}\otimes u$ form a morphism $\mathcal P_u:\mathcal P_M\to\mathcal P_{M'}$ of presheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules, and $\mathcal F_u:\mathcal F_M\to\mathcal F_{M'}$ is the unique $\mathcal O_X$-linear map with $\mathcal F_u\circ\sigma_M=\sigma_{M'}\circ\mathcal P_u$ (universal property of sheafification); in particular $\mathcal F_{u,X}\circ c_M=c_{M'}\circ u$. Moreover $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{id}_M}=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal F_M}$ and $\mathcal F_{v\circ u}=\mathcal F_v\circ\mathcal F_u$ for $R$-linear $u:M\to M'$, $v:M'\to M''$, so $M\mapsto\mathcal F_M$, $u\mapsto\mathcal F_u$ is a functor from $R$-modules to $\mathcal O_X$-modules. (Stacks, Modules, Lemma 01BH, construction (3), with $\alpha=\mathrm{id}_R$, and Definition 01BI.)

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01BH (lemma-construct-quasi-coherent-sheaves), construction (3) with alpha = id, and Definition 01BI (definition-sheaf-associated)

proof.text: *$\mathcal P_M$ is a presheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules.* $\mathcal O_X$ is a sheaf of commutative rings on the opens of $X$ [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism], so the restrictions $\rho^U_V:\mathcal O_X(U)\to\mathcal O_X(V)$ ($V\subseteq U$) are ring homomorphisms with $\rho^U_U=\mathrm{id}$ and $\rho^V_W\circ\rho^U_V=\rho^U_W$. The $R$-algebra structure of $\mathcal O_X(U)$ is $\rho^X_U$, and $\rho^U_V\circ\rho^X_U=\rho^X_V$, so every $\rho^U_V$ is an $R$-algebra homomorphism. Hence $\mathcal P_M(U)=\mathcal O_X(U)\otimes_RM$ is an $\mathcal O_X(U)$-module (the base change of $M$ along $R\to\mathcal O_X(U)$ [def-weil-module-base-change], tensor factors written in the other order), and the $R$-bilinear map $(a,m)\mapsto\rho^U_V(a)\otimes m$ induces the additive map $\rho^U_V\otimes\mathrm{id}_M:a\otimes m\mapsto\rho^U_V(a)\otimes m$ (universal property of $\otimes_R$; bilinearity uses only that $\rho^U_V$ is additive and $R$-linear). On generators $a\otimes m$: $(\rho^U_U\otimes\mathrm{id})=\mathrm{id}$, $(\rho^V_W\otimes\mathrm{id})(\rho^U_V\otimes\mathrm{id})=\rho^U_W\otimes\mathrm{id}$, so $\mathcal P_M$ is a presheaf of abelian groups; and for $b\in\mathcal O_X(U)$, $(\rho^U_V\otimes\mathrm{id})(b\cdot(a\otimes m))=\rho^U_V(ba)\otimes m=\rho^U_V(b)\cdot(\rho^U_V(a)\otimes m)$, i.e. the restriction maps are semilinear over $\rho^U_V$. By additivity these identities hold on all of $\mathcal P_M(U)$, so $\mathcal P_M$ is a presheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules in the sense of [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification].

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01BH (lemma-construct-quasi-coherent-sheaves), construction (3) and assertion (2) (functoriality), with alpha = id; Definition 01BI

proof.text: *$\mathcal F_M$ and $\sigma_M$ are well defined.* The opens of $X$ with inclusions, a family $\{U_j\subseteq U\}$ covering $U$ when $U=\bigcup_jU_j$, form a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] (fibre products are intersections), and $\mathcal O_X$ is a sheaf of rings on it. Applying [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] to the presheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules $\mathcal P_M$ of Step 1 gives the sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules $\mathcal F_M=\mathcal P_M^\#$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and the $\mathcal O_X$-linear map $\sigma_M:\mathcal P_M\to\mathcal F_M$, through which every $\mathcal O_X$-linear map from $\mathcal P_M$ to a sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules factors uniquely; $\mathcal F_M$ with $\sigma_M$ is determined up to unique isomorphism by this universal property. (In Stacks this is construction (3) of 01BH; its proof identifies it with $\pi^*M$ for $\pi:(X,\mathcal O_X)\to(\{*\},R)$, whose definition is this sheafification.)

source.place: Sheaves, Section ringed-spaces-functoriality-modules (pullback pi^* of modules defined as the sheafification of U -> O_X(U) tensor M), cited in the proof of Modules 01BH for F_1 = F_3

proof.text: *$c_M$ is $R$-linear.* The map $\iota:M\to\mathcal P_M(X)=R\otimes_RM$, $m\mapsto1\otimes m$, is additive, and $\iota(rm)=1\otimes rm=r\otimes m=r\cdot(1\otimes m)$ for $r\in R=\mathcal O_X(X)$ (the tensor is over $R$ and $\mathcal O_X(X)$ acts on the first factor); so $\iota$ is $R$-linear [def-weil-module-base-change]. The component $\sigma_{M,X}:\mathcal P_M(X)\to\mathcal F_M(X)=\Gamma(X,\mathcal F_M)$ is $\mathcal O_X(X)=R$-linear by Step 2. Hence $c_M=\sigma_{M,X}\circ\iota$ is $R$-linear, for the $R$-module structure of $\Gamma(X,\mathcal F_M)$ as an $\mathcal O_X(X)$-module.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01BH (lemma-construct-quasi-coherent-sheaves), construction (3) and assertion (2) (functoriality), with alpha = id; Definition 01BI

proof.text: *$\mathcal P_u$ is a morphism of presheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules, functorial in $u$.* For an $R$-linear $u:M\to M'$, $\mathcal P_{u,U}=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal O_X(U)}\otimes u:a\otimes m\mapsto a\otimes u(m)$ is the base change of $u$ to $\mathcal O_X(U)$, which is $\mathcal O_X(U)$-linear, with $\mathrm{id}\otimes\mathrm{id}_M=\mathrm{id}$ and $(\mathrm{id}\otimes v)(\mathrm{id}\otimes u)=\mathrm{id}\otimes(v\circ u)$ [def-weil-module-base-change]. It commutes with restrictions: both $(\rho^U_V\otimes\mathrm{id}_{M'})\circ(\mathrm{id}\otimes u)$ and $(\mathrm{id}\otimes u)\circ(\rho^U_V\otimes\mathrm{id}_M)$ send $a\otimes m$ to $\rho^U_V(a)\otimes u(m)$, and are additive. So $\mathcal P_u:\mathcal P_M\to\mathcal P_{M'}$ is a morphism of presheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], $\mathcal P_{\mathrm{id}_M}=\mathrm{id}$, $\mathcal P_{v\circ u}=\mathcal P_v\circ\mathcal P_u$, and $\mathcal P_{u,X}(1\otimes m)=1\otimes u(m)$.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01BH (lemma-construct-quasi-coherent-sheaves), construction (3) and assertion (2) (functoriality), with alpha = id; Definition 01BI

proof.text: *$\mathcal F_u$ exists, is unique and is functorial.* $\sigma_{M'}\circ\mathcal P_u:\mathcal P_M\to\mathcal F_{M'}$ is $\mathcal O_X$-linear (Steps 2 and 4) with target a sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules, so by the universal property of $\sigma_M$ [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] there is exactly one $\mathcal O_X$-linear $\mathcal F_u:\mathcal F_M\to\mathcal F_{M'}$ with $\mathcal F_u\circ\sigma_M=\sigma_{M'}\circ\mathcal P_u$. For $u=\mathrm{id}_M$, both $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{id}_M}$ and $\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal F_M}$ satisfy $\varphi\circ\sigma_M=\sigma_M=\sigma_M\circ\mathcal P_{\mathrm{id}_M}$, so they are equal by uniqueness. For $v:M'\to M''$: $(\mathcal F_v\circ\mathcal F_u)\circ\sigma_M=\mathcal F_v\circ\sigma_{M'}\circ\mathcal P_u=\sigma_{M''}\circ\mathcal P_v\circ\mathcal P_u=\sigma_{M''}\circ\mathcal P_{v\circ u}$ (Step 4), so $\mathcal F_v\circ\mathcal F_u=\mathcal F_{v\circ u}$ by uniqueness. Hence $M\mapsto\mathcal F_M$, $u\mapsto\mathcal F_u$ is a functor (Stacks 01BH (2), there via $\pi^*$).

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01BH (lemma-construct-quasi-coherent-sheaves), construction (3) and assertion (2) (functoriality), with alpha = id; Definition 01BI

proof.text: *Compatibility with the canonical section maps.* For $m\in M$, by Step 5 at the open $X$ and Step 4: $\mathcal F_{u,X}(c_M(m))=\mathcal F_{u,X}(\sigma_{M,X}(1\otimes m))=\sigma_{M',X}(\mathcal P_{u,X}(1\otimes m))=\sigma_{M',X}(1\otimes u(m))=c_{M'}(u(m))$. So $\mathcal F_{u,X}\circ c_M=c_{M'}\circ u$.
